बॉक्स ऑफिस पर आया 'रामायण' का तूफान, रिलीज से 10 दिन पहले ही उड़ा दिए होश! 🔥

नितेश तिवारी के निर्देशन में बन रही फिल्म Ramayana Part One ने रिलीज से 10 दिन पहले, 25 October तक Worldwide एडवांस बुकिंग में 20 करोड़ रुपये का आंकड़ा पार कर लिया है। 💥

Sacnilk की रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, अकेले भारत में फिल्म ने Day 1 के लिए 2 लाख से ज्यादा टिकट बेचकर 10 करोड़ रुपये कमाए हैं, जिसमें Hindi वर्जन की हिस्सेदारी 87% है।

Kannada वर्जन 1 करोड़ रुपये पार कर चुका है, वहीं Telugu वर्जन के सिर्फ 10-15 स्क्रीन खुलने के बावजूद 44 में से 4 शोज Houseful हो चुके हैं।

विदेशों में भी भारी क्रेज है; North America में 4 November के Paid previews से $550K और ओवरसीज रिलीज डे से $400K की कमाई दर्ज की गई है।

Namit Malhotra और Yash के प्रोडक्शन में बनी यह फिल्म 5 November 2026 को रिलीज होगी, जिसमें Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Yash और Sunny Deol मुख्य किरदारों में हैं। 🎬

क्या आप भी Ranbir Kapoor और Yash की इस ब्लॉकबस्टर फिल्म को देखने के लिए एक्साइटेड हैं? कमेंट्स में बताएं! 💬

ctx.title: Ramayana advance booking crosses  ₹20 crore 10 days before release; Ranbir Kapoor and Yash's film sees houseful shows in Telugu
ctx.summary: Ramayana has grossed over  ₹20 crore in pre-sales 10 days ahead of its release, with huge demand in Telugu states as well as North America.
ctx.text:
Advance bookings for Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana Part One are going steady after a blockbuster start on Dussehra. The pre-sales for the ambitious adaptation began 15 days before its scheduled release, ahead of Diwali. The first day a bumper response for the tickets. The pace his since plateaued, but the momentum remains positive for the big-budget spectacle.
Ramayana has reached the ₹ 10 crore mark in advance bookings in India alone, selling over 2 lakh tickets for its opening day domestically. Initially, the Hindi version was accounting for almost all of the pre-sales collections, but over the last two days, more Kannada and Telugu shows have begun to open. The Hindi version still accounts for 87% of the film’s advance bookings. The Kannada version, which is now open in around 100 screens, has crossed the ₹ 1 crore mark, with some centres already reporting up to 80% occupancy for the morning shows. The Telugu shows have opened in only around 10-15 screens, but are still hurtling towards the ₹ 40 lakh mark.
What has helped Ramayana’s case is the pre-sales buzz overseas. In North America, the film will have paid previews on November 4, the eve of its release. According to Sacnilk, the film has sold $550K in tickets for those paid previews. In addition, Ramayana has grossed $400K for the release day from overseas territories. This brings the film’s worldwide advance-booking gross to ₹ 20 crore by the end of October 25, ten days before its release.
Only a few regional Ramayana shows have opened for advance bookings so far. The Hindi version is already selling tickets for over 4200 shows across India for day 1. In comparison, the Kannada and Telugu versions have just over 400 shows combined. Yet, the Telugu version is seeing breakneck bookings. According to Sacnilk, four of the 44 Telugu shows are already houseful. On-the-ground tracking indicates that the number across languages may exceed a dozen after accounting for blocked seats.
Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part film. The film stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. The first part is scheduled for worldwide release on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2027. The films will release in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam across India.
Sony Pictures will handle global distribution, excluding India, while Dharma Productions will distribute the film in the Hindi-speaking market. The film is also planned for a worldwide IMAX release.
Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well.

A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism.

Work has led him to far off places like Japan and Jordan, as well as to the interiors of Haryana and the Indo-Pak border. He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. A Rotten Tomatoes Certified Film Critic, he is equally at home covering stories on ground as he is interviewing celebrities and studios, and sometimes prefers to shepherd teams in delivering traffic through the day.
